chapter_title: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables

zero_omission_notes.summary: Covers systems of two linear equations in two variables, graphical representation (intersecting, parallel, coincident lines), algebraic solutions (substitution, elimination), and consistency conditions based on coefficient ratios.

detailed_sections.full_explanation: a1 x + b1 y + c1 = 0 and a2 x + b2 y + c2 = 0. Intersecting (a1/a2 != b1/b2 -> unique solution), Coincident (a1/a2 = b1/b2 = c1/c2 -> infinite solutions), Parallel (a1/a2 = b1/b2 != c1/c2 -> no solution).

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Ratio Conditions
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: Unique: a1/a2 != b1/b2; Infinite: a1/a2 = b1/b2 = c1/c2; No solution: a1/a2 = b1/b2 != c1/c2

detailed_sections.full_explanation: Substitution: isolate one variable and substitute. Elimination: equalize coefficients of one variable by multiplication and add/subtract.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Elimination Choice
margin_notes_and_sidebars.full_content: Choose variable with simpler coefficients to minimize arithmetic errors.

diagrams_figures_and_maps.drawing_or_reading_instructions: Plot both linear equations on Cartesian coordinate plane.
diagrams_figures_and_maps.structural_or_conceptual_explanation: Geometrical proof of consistent vs inconsistent systems.

master_glossary_units_and_formulas.definition_or_meaning: Ratio tests to check system solvability.

textbook_exercises.question: Check if 5x - 4y + 8 = 0 and 7x + 6y - 9 = 0 intersect, are parallel, or coincident.
textbook_exercises.answer: a1/a2 = 5/7, b1/b2 = -4/6 = -2/3. Since 5/7 != -2/3, lines intersect at a unique point.

analytical_reasoning_questions.question: Sum of digits of a two-digit number is 9. Nine times this number is twice the number obtained by reversing digits. Find the number.

comprehensive_long_answers.question: Solve graphically: 2x + y = 6 and 2x - y = 2. Find vertices of triangle formed by these lines and x-axis.
comprehensive_long_answers.answer: 2x + y = 6 passes through (0,6), (3,0). 2x - y = 2 passes through (0,-2), (1,0). Intersection point is (2,2). Triangle vertices on x-axis are (1,0), (3,0), and (2,2).

common_misconceptions_and_pitfalls.common_error_or_misconception: Comparing ratios without arranging constants on the same side of equal sign.
common_misconceptions_and_pitfalls.correct_fact_or_method: Always rewrite equations as ax + by + c = 0 before extracting c1 and c2.
